first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, and inherited evidence indicates that shorter onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. I will verify the directly relevant onboarding result and the pricing result because competitor pricing is consequential but may trade durable qualified revenue for lower-value acquisition. Pending verification, a bounded onboarding simplification experiment is the strongest sustainable-revenue response.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. Verified evidence shows shorter onboarding raised completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%, directly addressing both current declines while supporting durable account value. Do not use promotional pricing: although it increased qualified revenue initially, the discounted cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Long-term revenue effects beyond 30 days remain uncertain, so monitor downstream qualification, retention, and expansion outcomes.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. It has verified evidence of higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, addressing the activation and onboarding declines with a durable-value mechanism. Do not pivot to promotional pricing solely in response to the competitor: the verified discount experiment increased initial qualified revenue but reduced 30-day retention by 12% and did not survive the first renewal cycle. The deeper competitive cut may change the severity of near-term SMB churn, but there is no verified evidence that matching it sustainably retains value; monitor price-sensitive SMB churn closely while the experiment runs.
